elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: New Section 11.4: "the customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One". The element is disjunctive (Agreement or Order Form) and this Agreement has no Order Form structure, so the Agreement-level right suffices.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: 11.4 fixes the notice at "thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One" - exactly the preferred ceiling, in writing.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: 11.4: "Commerce One shall refund pro rata any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination." The refund is expressly pro rata (not merely a post-termination-period refund) and is owed by Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: 11.4: "Commerce One shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the initial five (5) year term or any renewal term." Section 11.2 retains only for-cause/insolvency termination, and the 11.1 notice of intent not to renew takes effect at expiration of the then-current term, so it is natural-term non-renewal under RENEWAL rather than a mid-term convenience right.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: 11.4 sets 30 days' notice, which is outside (and better than) the 60-90 day fallback band; the fallback band is literally not satisfied.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: no early-termination fee, penalty, or accelerated-payment mechanic is imposed anywhere in Section 11 for a convenience exit, so the cap condition does not apply.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Satisfied a fortiori - 11.4 denies Commerce One any convenience right during the initial or any renewal term, so it cannot terminate for convenience mid-term; only the 11.1 end-of-term non-renewal mechanic remains, whose effect is expressly tied to expiration of the then-current term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: Vendor has no convenience termination right at all under 11.4, so no notice period is required of it. The 30-day notice in 11.1 is non-renewal at term end, assessed under RENEWAL.

reasons: All four preferred elements are met in operative language by new Section 11.4 (30 days' written notice, pro rata refund of prepaid fees, and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during the initial and renewal terms), so the position is complete at the preferred level.

Minimality fails on the opening words of 11.4: "Corio is the customer under this Agreement, and the customer may terminate...". No checklist element requires a definitional statement of who the customer is; a direct grant naming the party ("Corio may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice...") reaches the same result without adding a new interpretive term. Repair: delete "Corio is the customer under this Agreement, and the customer" and substitute "Corio".

Secondary risk from the same extra wording: Section 1.6 defines CUSTOMER(S) as Corio's own customers, so asserting that "Corio is the customer under this Agreement" invites an argument about the defined term even though lowercase is used. Deleting the sentence per the repair above removes the risk entirely.

Intent is preserved: Sections 11.1-11.3 are untouched, the for-cause and insolvency exits, survival list, Customer-continuity rights and support/payment mechanics all survive, no cross-reference is left dangling, and no retained sentence contradicts 11.4.
Fallback is not independently satisfied only because the notice period is 30 days rather than 60-90; that is irrelevant since the preferred level is complete and more favourable to us.
